title: Lightweight Fault Isolation: Practical, Efficient, and Secure Software Sandboxing
problem: Software-based fault isolation systems must efficiently isolate untrusted code while balancing performance, trusted code base size, and scalability, particularly for ARM64 systems used in cloud and serverless computing.
motivation: Cloud and serverless computing require systems to run untrusted code with low latency and minimal context switch overhead.
method: LFI supports tens of thousands of 4GiB sandboxes in a single address space through compiler-independent binary instrumentation. Full software isolation of loads, stores, and jumps is enforced via static verification with a small verifier reducing TCB. The system includes Spectre attack hardening and supports language exceptions and SIMD features.
key_novelty: First practical multi-sandbox SFI scheme for ARM64 achieving 7% runtime overhead while supporting tens of thousands of sandboxes with minimal trusted code base.
contributions: Multi-sandbox SFI design for ARM64 with 7% SPEC 2017 runtime overhead
Compiler-independent implementation with small static verifier for TCB minimization
Spectre attack hardening for software-based isolation
Broad software support for exceptions, SIMD, and multiple languages

metrics.other: 7% runtime overhead on SPEC 2017; supports tens of thousands of 4GiB sandboxes
